newsitem.title: USA: CSCE nearby coffee sinks as Colombia strike ends.
newsitem.headline: CSCE nearby coffee sinks as Colombia strike ends.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures settled mostly lower on Friday, pressured by an afternoon round of speculative selling amid news a six-day truckers' strike in Colombia was called off, traders said.
"They settled the strike in Colombia," said Smith Barney analyst Walt Spilka, "so, the market's giving back some of what it has gained on that news."

Prices ping-ponged on both sides of unchanged throughout the day, with the July, September and December 1997 contracts setting new life-of-contract highs during the session before the late-session sell-off.

After hitting a fresh high of 203.50 cents per lb, most-active July futures closed at down 4.95 cents, at 193.25 cents, just off the session low of 192.50 cents. Spot May finished down 3.40, to 216.35, while the outer months ended 4.30 lower to 6.00 higher.

Coffee prices headed lower at the outset, after a weak showing overnight in the London robusta market. But the New York market managed to bounce off key support levels, inspiring a bout of chart-driven buying.

Traders said July's breach of $2 per pound -- a crucial psychological level -- triggered technical buy orders. July quickly reached a new contract high of 203.50 cents, before some speculative profit-taking cut into gains, they said.
Some analysts said news late Friday that Colombia's main truck drivers' union agreed to end the work stoppage is likely to be a temporary setback.
With arabica inventories near historically low levels in the U.S., and uncertainty about the size of many Latin American crops, they said the futures market remained well supported.
"The end of the Colombia strike really should not matter," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "There are so many other bullish fundamental factors."
The nearby May/July switch, a barometer of nearby availability, widened to 23.10 today from 21.55 at the close on Thursday.
After Friday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell 1,747 60-kg bags, to 48,603 bags as of April 24. There were 3,815 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
The day's volume was moderate, at an estimated 8,224 lots.
